title: Python AI-app static analysis: what catches what
excerpt: We added Python AI-app regex prefilters to getdebug and benchmarked against Bandit, Semgrep, and (attempted) vulnhuntr. Here's where each tool actually catches things — and where they don't.
content_html:
getdebug CLI 0.4.0 ships Python AI-app regex prefilters alongside the JS/TS ones that landed in 0.3.0. Five categories: prompt-injection, unsafe-role-merge, pii-in-prompt, unbounded-stream, unsafe-tool-output. All deterministic. No LLM call. The default getdebug analyze . on a Python repo runs in milliseconds, costs zero, and now covers Python AI-app anti-patterns alongside the secrets + dependency-CVE passes it always ran.

The interesting part isn't the patterns themselves — they're straightforward regex on familiar SDK idioms (messages=[{"role": "system"...}], stream=True, subprocess.run(tool_call.input.command)). The interesting part is the benchmark we ran while developing them, against the three other tools anyone would compare us to.

The four tools, the honest map

Bandit (PyCQA) is the Python-OSS standard security linter. Hand-written rules. Free, fast, no LLM. Python only.

Semgrep is multi-language SAST with community rule packs. Hand-written rules. Free, fast, no LLM. Same product shape as getdebug.

vulnhuntr (Protect AI, open source) is the stated category leader for AI-app static analysis. LLM-driven, Python-only, entry-point-detection based.

getdebug is what we ship: pattern-based regex prefilters in JS/TS + Python now, plus an optional local-LLM SAST pass via Ollama (free, on-device) and a hosted LLM SAST pass via Claude (paid). The Python additions in 0.4.0 are the regex layer specifically.

Test 1 — paired vulnerable/safe fixtures (10 files)

We wrote 5 vulnerable + 5 safe Python AI-app fixtures, one pair per category. Same shape as our existing JS/TS corpus. All four tools ran on the same set.

Tool        TP  FP  FN   Precision  Recall
getdebug     5   1   0    83%        100%
bandit       1   1   4    50%        20%
semgrep      1   1   4    50%        20%
vulnhuntr    —   —   —    (0 files selected; see below)

Bandit and Semgrep both fire on the unsafe-tool-output fixture via their generic subprocess.run(shell=True) rules — that's a true positive on the vulnerable variant. But they also fire on the safe variant of the same fixture, the one where the model output is mapped through an allowlist before reaching the shell:

# Safe pattern — Bandit + Semgrep both flag this as a FP
ALLOWED = {"hosts": "cat /etc/hosts", "uptime": "uptime"}
def handle(tool_call):
    cmd = ALLOWED.get(tool_call.input.tag)
    if not cmd: return "rejected"
    return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True).stdout

Neither tool knows that cmd came from a static dict, not from the model. They see shell=True and fire. getdebug's regex requires the tool_call.input.X / block.input.X reference to appear in the sink arg, which narrows the false-positive surface the generic SAST tools don't. Honesty update: the scanPyShellToolArg detector added in 0.5.5 now fires a CRITICAL on this same safe fixture — it sees tool_call.input.tag reaching a shell=True sink and can't tell the value was routed through the static allowlist first. Re-running the corpus on 0.5.5 scores getdebug at 5 TP / 1 FP / 0 FN (83% precision) on this set, not the clean sweep the original 0.4.0 numbers showed. Tightening this allowlist case is tracked.

Both tools miss the other four behavioural categories entirely — pii-in-prompt, unsafe-role-merge, prompt-injection, unbounded-stream. They aren't designed for them; the rule packs don't contain patterns for {"role": "system", "content": f"...{'$'}{name}..."}. That's our addition.

Test 2 — the real-world signal/noise check

Synthetic fixtures lock the behaviour in. The real test for a security scanner is what it does on actual code. We ran all three (working) tools against simonw/llm — Simon Willison's clean, well-maintained CLI for talking to LLMs, 49 Python files (commit 0d593ea; raw tool outputs in bench/realworld/).

Tool        Total findings    Signal
bandit      1,261            1,228 are 'assert_used' (pytest);
                              zero AI-app coverage
semgrep     3                3 generic-SAST hits;
                              zero AI-app coverage
getdebug    7                6 AI-app findings (1 prompt-injection,
                              5 unbounded-stream) + 1 borderline role-merge

Bandit's 1,261 findings on this 49-file codebase is almost entirely noise: 1,228 of them are assert_used warnings on pytest assertions. This is a long-standing Bandit complaint — the default config flags every assert as a security smell because asserts disappear under python -O. For a production app where you opt-out of -O optimisation (which is almost everyone), this is pure noise.

Semgrep's 3 findings are real but generic: an exec() usage flagged in cli.py (intentional for the plugin system), a missing-integrity attribute on a static HTML asset, and a non-literal import. None of these are AI-app specific.

Six of getdebug's seven findings are AI-app categorized: one prompt-injection (the CLI's template feature concatenating two user-supplied strings) and five unbounded-stream hits in the OpenAI plugin (each stream=True with no with block or timeout in scope). Both arguable as TPs depending on threat model — this is a single-user CLI, so the prompt-injection between two CLI-user inputs is a stretch, and the library delegates stream-management to its consumer. The seventh, a role-merge on {"role": role}, is a borderline false positive — the role echoes the API's own streaming response, not request input — the kind of thing you'd triage away. Everything is flagged HIGH / MEDIUM, not CRITICAL, with context to triage. The CLI suppresses findings with a .getdebug-ignore file (inline // getdebug:ignore annotations are a hosted-scan feature).

About vulnhuntr

vulnhuntr is the stated category leader for LLM-driven AI-app static analysis, so we re-checked the current release. Two findings, and we want to be fair about both:

  • It runs. vulnhuntr 1.2.2 installs and starts cleanly on Python 3.11 — the older ModuleNotFoundError is gone. Like any LLM-driven tool it needs a provider (an API key, or a local Ollama via --llm ollama).
  • But it sees nothing here. Its file-selection heuristic targets “network-exposed” entry points, and simonw/llm is a CLI, not a web app — so vulnhuntr selects zero files to analyse and surfaces nothing on this repo. Confirmed with its own --dry-run (0 files, $0.00, no key needed).

So vulnhuntr isn't broken — it's scoped to web-app entry points, which makes it a no-op on a CLI library like this one. Different tool, different target: getdebug's AI-app prefilters run on any Python that touches an LLM, web app or not. That's the gap we're shipping into.

What this means for you

If you ship a Python app that calls an LLM — chat wrapper, agent framework, tool-calling backend, batch summariser — you should run all three:

  • bandit -r . for general Python security hygiene (turn off assert_used via .bandit config first).
  • semgrep --config auto . for cross-language SAST coverage.
  • npx @getdebug/cli@0.4.0 analyze . for the AI-app behavioural patterns the other two don't target.

They're complementary. None of them subsume the others. The first two catch general SAST and Python hygiene; getdebug catches the “serialised the whole user object into the LLM prompt” class of bugs that you can't hand-write a sustainable rule for in generic SAST without painful ergonomics.

Reproduce every number on this page at getdebug.dev/bench. Corpus, methodology, and harness are open — CodeSecBench on GitHub.

And as always: if you see a result you can't reproduce, or a pattern getdebug should catch but doesn't, the corpus is open — PRs welcome, harness is reproducible, methodology is documented. That's the whole point of doing the benchmark in public.

try it

npx @getdebug/cli@0.4.0 analyze .

Or via Homebrew: brew install getdebug-ai/tap/getdebug

— Fafa Agbetsise / Founder, getdebug.dev

blocks.html_en: Semgrep's 3 findings are real but generic: an exec() usage flagged in cli.py (intentional for the plugin system), a missing-integrity attribute on a static HTML asset, and a non-literal import. None of these are AI-app specific.

blocks.html_en: Six of getdebug's seven findings are AI-app categorized: one prompt-injection (the CLI's template feature concatenating two user-supplied strings) and five unbounded-stream hits in the OpenAI plugin (each stream=True with no with block or timeout in scope). Both arguable as TPs depending on threat model — this is a single-user CLI, so the prompt-injection between two CLI-user inputs is a stretch, and the library delegates stream-management to its consumer. The seventh, a role-merge on {"role": role}, is a borderline false positive — the role echoes the API's own streaming response, not request input — the kind of thing you'd triage away. Everything is flagged HIGH / MEDIUM, not CRITICAL, with context to triage. The CLI suppresses findings with a .getdebug-ignore file (inline // getdebug:ignore annotations are a hosted-scan feature).

sentences.en: — Fafa Agbetsise / Founder, getdebug.dev
sentences.zh: — Fafa Lifecycle / getdebug.dev 创始人

content_html_zh:
getdebug CLI 0.4.0 附带了 Python AI-app 正则表达式预过滤器以及 0.3.0 中的 JS/TS 预过滤器。 五个类别：提示注入、不安全角色合并、pii-in-prompt、无界流、不安全工具输出。 都是确定性的。 没有LLM电话。 默认 getdebug 分析 。 在 Python 存储库上的运行时间为几毫秒，成本为零，现在涵盖了 Python AI 应用程序反模式以及它始终运行的秘密 + 依赖项 CVE 传递。

有趣的部分不是模式本身 - 它们是熟悉的 SDK 惯用语的简单正则表达式（messages=[{"role": "system"...}]、stream=True、subprocess.run(tool_call.input.command)）。 有趣的部分是我们在开发它们时运行的基准，与任何人都会将我们进行比较的其他三个工具进行比较。

四种工具，诚实的地图

Bandit (PyCQA) 是 Python-OSS 标准安全 linter。 手写规则。 免费、快速、无需法学硕士。 仅限Python。

Semgrep 是带有社区规则包的多语言 SAST。 手写规则。 免费、快速、无需法学硕士。 与 getdebug 相同的产品形状。

vulnhuntr（Protect AI，开源）是 AI 应用静态分析领域的领先者。 LLM 驱动、仅 Python、基于入口点检测。

getdebug 是我们提供的：现在采用 JS/TS + Python 的基于模式的正则表达式预过滤器，加上可选的通过 Ollama 的本地 LLM SAST 通行证（免费，设备上）和通过 Claude 的托管 LLM SAST 通行证（付费）。 0.4.0 中的 Python 添加具体是正则表达式层。

测试 1 — 配对易受攻击/安全的装置（10 个文件）

我们编写了 5 个易受攻击的 + 5 个安全的 Python AI 应用装置，每个类别一对。 与我们现有的 JS/TS 语料库形状相同。 所有四个工具都在同一组上运行。

Tool        TP  FP  FN   Precision  Recall
getdebug     5   1   0    83%        100%
bandit       1   1   4    50%        20%
semgrep      1   1   4    50%        20%
vulnhuntr    —   —   —    (0 files selected; see below)

Bandit 和 Semgrep 都通过其通用的 subprocess.run(shell=True) 规则触发不安全工具输出装置——这对易受攻击的变体来说是一个真正的积极结果。 但它们也会触发同一装置的安全变体，即模型输出在到达 shell 之前通过允许列表进行映射的变体：

# Safe pattern — Bandit + Semgrep both flag this as a FP
ALLOWED = {"hosts": "cat /etc/hosts", "uptime": "uptime"}
def handle(tool_call):
    cmd = ALLOWED.get(tool_call.input.tag)
    if not cmd: return "rejected"
    return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True).stdout

这两个工具都不知道 cmd 来自静态字典，而不是来自模型。 他们看到 shell=True 并着火。 getdebug 的正则表达式要求 tool_call.input.X / block.input.X 引用出现在接收器参数中，这会缩小通用 SAST 工具所没有的误报范围。 诚实更新：0.5.5 中添加的 scanPyShellToolArg 检测器现在在同一个安全装置上触发 CRITICAL — 它看到 tool_call.input.tag 到达 shell=True 接收器，并且无法判断该值首先通过静态允许列表路由。 在 0.5.5 上重新运行语料库，getdebug 的得分为 5 TP / 1 FP / 0 FN（83% 精度），而不是原始 0.4.0 数字显示的一网打尽。 跟踪收紧此许可名单的情况。

这两种工具完全忽略了其他四种行为类别——pii-in-prompt、不安全角色合并、提示注入、无界流。 它们不是为他们设计的；而是为他们设计的。规则包不包含 {"role": "system", "content": f"...{'$'}{name}..."} 的模式。 这是我们的补充。

测试 2 — 真实世界的信号/噪声检查

合成装置锁定行为。 对安全扫描器的真正测试是它对实际代码的作用。 我们针对 simonw/llm 运行了所有三个（工作）工具——Simon Willison 干净、维护良好的 CLI，用于与 LLM 对话，49 个 Python 文件（提交 0d593ea；原始工具输出在 bench/realworld/ 中）。

Tool        Total findings    Signal
bandit      1,261            1,228 are 'assert_used' (pytest);
                              zero AI-app coverage
semgrep     3                3 generic-SAST hits;
                              zero AI-app coverage
getdebug    7                6 AI-app findings (1 prompt-injection,
                              5 unbounded-stream) + 1 borderline role-merge

Bandit 在这个 49 文件代码库上的 1,261 个发现几乎完全是噪音：其中 1,228 个是关于 pytest 断言的 assert_used 警告。 这是一个长期存在的 Bandit 抱怨——默认配置将每个断言标记为安全气味，因为断言在 python -O 下消失。 对于您选择退出 -O 优化（几乎所有人）的生产应用程序来说，这纯粹是噪音。

Semgrep 的 3 个发现是真实但通用的：cli.py 中标记的 exec() 用法（针对插件系统）、静态 HTML 资源上缺少完整性属性以及非文字导入。 这些都不是特定于人工智能应用程序的。

getdebug 的 7 个发现中有 6 个属于 AI 应用分类：1 个提示注入（CLI 的模板功能连接两个用户提供的字符串）和 OpenAI 插件中的 5 个无界流命中（每个流 = True，范围内没有块或超时）。 根据威胁模型，两者都可以作为 TP - 这是一个单用户 CLI，因此两个 CLI 用户输入之间的提示注入是一个延伸，并且库将流管理委托给其使用者。 第七种，{“role”：role} 上的角色合并，是一种边缘误报——该角色回显 API 自己的流响应，而不是请求输入——您应该将其分类。 一切都被标记为“高”/“中”，而不是“严重”，并带有上下文进行分类。 CLI 使用 .getdebug-ignore 文件抑制发现结果（内联 // getdebug:ignore 注释是托管扫描功能）。

关于 vulnhuntr

vulnhuntr 是 LLM 驱动的 AI 应用静态分析领域的领先者，因此我们重新检查了当前版本。 有两个发现，我们希望公平对待这两个发现：

  • 它运行了。 vulnhuntr 1.2.2 在 Python 3.11 上安装并正常启动 — 旧的 ModuleNotFoundError 消失了。 与任何 LLM 驱动的工具一样，它需要一个提供者（API 密钥，或通过 --llm ollama 提供本地 Ollama）。
  • 但它在这里什么也没看到。 它的文件选择启发式目标是“网络公开”入口点，并且 simonw/llm 是 CLI，而不是 Web 应用程序 - 因此 vulnhuntr 选择零个文件进行分析，并且在此存储库上不显示任何内容。 用它自己的 --dry-run 确认（0 个文件，0.00 美元，不需要密钥）。

所以 vulnhuntr 并没有被破坏——它的范围仅限于 Web 应用程序入口点，这使得它在像这样的 CLI 库上无法进行操作。 不同的工具，不同的目标：getdebug 的 AI 应用程序预过滤器可以在任何涉及 LLM、Web 应用程序或不涉及的 Python 上运行。 这就是我们要进入的差距。

这对您意味着什么

如果您发布一个调用 LLM 的 Python 应用程序（聊天包装器、代理框架、工具调用后端、批量摘要器），您应该运行所有三个：

  • 强盗-r。 为了一般的Python安全卫生（首先通过.bandit配置关闭assert_used）。
  • semgrep --config auto 。 用于跨语言 SAST 覆盖。
  • npx @getdebug/cli@0.4.0 分析 。 对于其他两个不针对的人工智能应用程序行为模式。

它们是互补的。 它们都不包含其他的。 前两个遵循一般 SAST 和 Python 规范； getdebug 捕获“将整个用户对象序列化到 LLM 提示符”类别的错误，您无法在通用 SAST 中手写可持续的规则，而不需要痛苦的人体工程学。

在 getdebug.dev/bench 上复制此页面上的每个数字。 语料库、方法论和工具都是开放的——GitHub 上的 CodeSecBench。

与往常一样：如果您看到无法重现的结果，或者 getdebug 应该捕获但没有捕获的模式，则语料库是开放的 - 欢迎 PR，工具是可重现的，方法是有记录的。 这就是公开进行基准测试的全部意义。

try it

npx @getdebug/cli@0.4.0 分析 。

或者通过 Homebrew：brew install getdebug-ai/tap/getdebug

— Fafa Lifecycle / getdebug.dev 创始人
